name: Carpets, handicrafts and artisan workshops

problems.words: Advances given to karigars and I don't know how much work is done against them
quick_ideas: List each advance against the piece it was for — shows what's outstanding
Ask for a progress photo before the next advance — ties money to work.

workzap_build.text: an advance ledger per artisan role or contractor, showing advance versus value of work done.

problems.free_stops: How work value is measured against advances is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many advanced pieces are still unfinished at week end, so you can see cash tied up in pending work.
Give one staff member one notebook for advances and completed pieces, so each new payment links to visible progress.

problems.words: Contractor says 30 carpets are on looms but I can't verify
quick_ideas: Ask for a dated photo of each piece on the loom — gives you proof
List every piece with design, size and start date — one picture of WIP.

workzap_build.text: an artisan WIP board with progress photos and expected completion for every piece.

problems.ask_first: How do updates reach you today?
problems.free_stops: The update routine for home-based artisans is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk the looms and count pieces actually in progress against the contractor's claim, so you know the true work on hand.
Give one person the job of noting each loom's active piece in one notebook, so contractor updates match workshop reality.

problems.words: Export deadline missed and nobody told me
quick_ideas: Set milestones for each export order (on loom, off loom, washing, inspection) — shows slippage early
Check the slowest pieces each week — time to react.

workzap_build.text: an order tracker with milestones and alerts when progress lags.

problems.ask_first: Are most orders custom or from ready stock?
problems.free_stops: Milestone set-up is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each export order's current stage on one page every afternoon, so missed handovers show before the deadline passes.
Give one person the job of updating delayed pieces at closing time, so late work reaches you before shipment is missed.

problems.words: Wool and dye given to artisans and some disappears
quick_ideas: Record what's issued per piece — makes each issue accountable
Record what comes back — shows the gap.

workzap_build.text: a raw-material issue log per piece with returns recorded.

problems.ask_first: Who buys the wool, you or the artisans?
problems.free_stops: The issue and return rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare wool and dye issued with what each carpet returns in leftovers once, so loss around specific pieces becomes visible.
Give one person one return spot for leftover wool and dye, so missing material is noticed when work comes back.

quick_ideas: Do your own inspection before the buyer's — catches defects first
Photograph each piece at inspection — evidence for later.

workzap_build.text: a pre-shipment inspection checklist with photos per piece.

problems.ask_first: What do buyers reject most often?
problems.free_stops: The checklist content is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count which rejection issues repeat across recently returned pieces, so you can see the defect hurting inspections most.
Give one person the job of checking finished pieces in one corner before packing, so buyer rejections are caught earlier.

problems.words: Stock of finished carpets isn't photographed or catalogued
quick_ideas: Photograph and measure your finished pieces once — buyers can see what's available
Note location of each — finding them gets quicker.

workzap_build.text: a finished-stock catalogue with photos, sizes, knot count and location, shareable as a link.

problems.ask_first: How do buyers see your stock now?
problems.free_stops: The catalogue set-up is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk the finished stock and note which pieces have no photo or size written, so selling time is not wasted searching.
Give one person one notebook for finished pieces and their storage spots, so staff can find saleable stock quickly.

problems.words: Online orders come from Etsy, Instagram, WhatsApp and the website
quick_ideas: Put every channel's orders into one list — nothing missed
Make one person responsible — clear ownership.

workzap_build.text: a unified order inbox for Etsy, Instagram, website and WhatsApp.

problems.free_stops: Channel connections are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many orders arrived from each sales channel this week, so you see where missed follow ups are most likely.
Give one person one daily order list from every channel, so dispatch work starts from one complete record.

problems.words: International customers ask at night and we reply late
quick_ideas: Clear overnight questions first thing each morning — buyers hear back faster
Keep answers to common questions ready — speeds replies.

workzap_build.text: after-hours acknowledgement collecting buyer questions for the morning, with response times tracked.

problems.ask_first: Which time zones are your buyers in?
problems.free_stops: The message flow is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note how many overnight buyer messages are still unanswered by midday, so you can see the morning reply backlog clearly.
Give one person the job of clearing night enquiries at opening time, so overseas buyers hear back while they are still active.

problems.words: Everything depends on me — designs, buyers, payments
quick_ideas: List decisions only you make — shows what could be handed over
Hand one area to a trusted person — frees your time.

workzap_build.text: a morning read of pieces in progress, overdue pieces, advances outstanding, stock value and open orders.

problems.ask_first: Which area takes most of your time?
problems.free_stops: Which figures and handovers to set up is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note every decision that waited for you this week, so you can see which area stalls when you are busy.
Give one person one fixed handover time for design, buyer or payment updates, so routine decisions stop waiting for your attention.

never_say: No labour-law, minimum-wage or artisan contract advice.
Child-labour concerns: never help hide them; point to emergency services and child-protection helplines if a child is at risk.
No customs, export-regulation, tariff or authentication advice.
Never help pass machine-made as hand-made, fake antiques, false origin labels or certificates, or under-invoice exports; decline.
No artisans' names, IDs, villages or phone numbers; roles and counts only.

sample_reply.person: Koi tareeqa batao. Karigaron ko peshgi deta hoon lekin pata nahi chalta kitna kaam hua hai.
sample_reply.pi:
Bilkul, is ka hal mumkin hai, aur pehla qadam aasan hai.
Pehle, har peshgi ko us piece ke saath likhein jis ke liye di gayi, taake pata ho kitna baqi hai.
Doosra, agli peshgi se pehle loom par piece ki tareekh wali photo mangwayein, taake paisa kaam se jude.
Pakke hal ke liye Workzap ye banwa sakta hai: peshgi ledger aur WIP board jo har piece ki progress photos ke saath dikhaye ke kis ka kitna kaam hua aur kitni peshgi baqi hai.
